questions.q: In a community in Ijebu-Ode, many people develop rice-water stools and severe dehydration after drinking water from a shallow well close to a soakaway. Which measure will most directly reduce the spread of this disease?
options: Boil or chlorinate the well water before drinking
Spray the surroundings with insecticide to kill houseflies
Give all patients an antimalarial drug
Allow the well water to stand overnight before drinking
questions.explanation: Cholera is spread mainly by drinking water or food contaminated with Vibrio cholerae from faeces, and boiling or chlorinating water kills the bacteria. Letting water stand overnight does not reliably make it safe, while antimalarial drugs and spraying for houseflies do not remove the cholera pathogen from drinking water.

questions.q: A cassava farmer in Nsukka steps on a rusty nail while working on the farm. Which action is most important to prevent tetanus?
options: Take a painkiller and continue farm work
Clean the wound and seek medical attention for tetanus prophylaxis
Apply palm oil to the wound and cover it tightly
Wash the foot with cold water and wait for the wound to dry
questions.explanation: Tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani spores in soil entering wounds, so cleaning the wound and getting prompt medical care with tetanus vaccine or immunoglobulin is important. Applying palm oil, taking only painkillers, or waiting for the wound to dry does not remove the spores or provide immunity.

questions.q: A student in Ibadan places a drop of red ink at the bottom of a beaker of clear water. The red colour spreads slowly through the water. Which change would make the colour spread faster?
options: Cool the water before adding the ink
Warm the water before adding the ink
Add the ink gently without disturbing the water
Use a taller beaker with the same water
questions.explanation: Diffusion is faster at higher temperature because the ink and water particles have more kinetic energy and move more quickly. Cooling the water slows diffusion, while using a taller beaker or adding ink gently does not increase the movement of particles.

questions.q: A woman in Ibadan has blood group AB, and her husband has blood group O. What is the probability that their child will have blood group A?
questions.explanation: The mother with blood group AB produces I^A and I^B gametes in equal numbers, while the father with group O produces only i gametes. A child receives I^A i in half the cases, and this genotype gives blood group A.

questions.q: A student in Bauchi finds an adult animal with an exoskeleton, jointed appendages and three pairs of legs. To which class does the animal belong?
questions.explanation: Adult insects have three pairs of jointed legs and a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen. Arachnids have four pairs of legs, while crustaceans and myriapods have many more legs or different body organisation.

questions.q: A farmer in Zaria notices that a crop seedling has one cotyledon and its mature leaves have parallel veins. The crop is best described as a
questions.explanation: One cotyledon and parallel leaf venation are characteristic features of monocotyledons. Dicotyledons have two cotyledons and usually reticulate venation, while gymnosperms bear seeds in cones and pteridophytes reproduce by spores.

questions.q: A student in Ogbomoso is asked to select a pair of arthropods from a collection. Which pair should the student select?
questions.explanation: The housefly and centipede both have jointed appendages and an exoskeleton, which are features of arthropods. A snail is a mollusc, an earthworm is an annelid, a tapeworm is a flatworm, a roundworm is a nematode, a starfish is an echinoderm, and a hydra is a cnidarian.

questions.q: A weightlifter in Ilorin bends his forearm at the elbow. The structure that attaches the biceps muscle to the radius is a
questions.explanation: A tendon attaches a muscle to a bone, so the biceps is attached to the radius by a tendon. A ligament joins bone to bone, cartilage reduces friction at joint surfaces, and the synovial membrane secretes lubricating fluid.

questions.q: A patient in Lagos has a urine test showing a large amount of protein. Which part of the kidney is most likely damaged?
questions.explanation: Protein molecules are normally too large to pass through the glomerular filtration membrane, so their presence in urine suggests damage to the glomerulus. The loop of Henle and collecting duct mainly adjust water and salt content after filtration has occurred.

questions.q: Which part of the brain regulates body temperature and the sensation of hunger?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the homeostatic control centre that regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst and several hormonal activities. The cerebrum controls voluntary activities, the cerebellum coordinates balance and muscular movement, and the medulla oblongata controls vital involuntary reflexes.

questions.q: A woman in Aba has a high blood calcium level. Which hormone lowers the calcium concentration in her blood?
questions.explanation: Calcitonin, secreted by the thyroid gland, promotes the deposition of calcium in bones and therefore lowers blood calcium concentration. Parathormone raises blood calcium, insulin lowers blood glucose, and thyroxine controls the general metabolic rate.

questions.q: A biology student in Ilesa examines an organelle made of flattened membrane sacs and small vesicles. Which function is most closely associated with this organelle?
options: Digestion of worn-out organelles by hydrolytic enzymes
Assembly of amino acids into polypeptide chains
Modification and packaging of proteins for secretion
Synthesis of ATP during oxidative phosphorylation
questions.explanation: The description matches the Golgi apparatus, which modifies and packages proteins and other materials into vesicles for secretion. ATP synthesis occurs in mitochondria, while hydrolytic digestion of worn-out organelles is a lysosomal function.

questions.q: A section of the small intestine from a goat in Makurdi contains several types of tissue working together for absorption. The small intestine is best described as
questions.explanation: The small intestine is made of different tissues—epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous—working together to perform absorption, so it is an organ. A tissue is a group of similar cells, while an organ system is a group of organs working together.

questions.q: In a pond near Epe, algae contain 20,000 kJ of energy. If energy is transferred along the food chain algae → mosquito larvae → small fish and 10% passes to the next trophic level at each step, how much energy is available to the small fish?
questions.explanation: At each trophic level only 10% of the energy passes on: mosquito larvae receive 20,000 × 0.10 = 2,000 kJ, and small fish receive 2,000 × 0.10 = 200 kJ. The 2,000 kJ value is the energy available to mosquito larvae, not to small fish.

questions.q: Farmers near Yankari notice that soil on a sloping field is being washed away after the vegetation is cleared. Which practice is most suitable for reducing soil erosion on the field?
options: Planting cover crops and retaining vegetation along the slope
Covering the field with a concrete slab
Allowing cattle to graze the field throughout the year
Burning the remaining grasses before planting
questions.explanation: Cover crops and vegetation along the slope reduce the speed of run-off and hold soil particles with their roots. Burning or overgrazing removes protective cover and exposes the soil, while a concrete slab is not a practical farm conservation measure.

questions.q: Which term best describes a pond in Badagry together with its water, dissolved salts, duckweed, tadpoles and kingfishers?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem consists of all living organisms in an area together with their non-living surroundings, interacting as a unit. A community contains only the living organisms, a population is one species, and a habitat is the place where organisms live.

questions.q: A patient in Aba has a blockage that prevents bile from entering the small intestine. Which process is most directly impaired?
options: Emulsification of fats into smaller droplets
Absorption of water in the large intestine
questions.explanation: Bile emulsifies fats into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase action. Starch and protein digestion depend mainly on amylase and proteases, while water absorption in the large intestine is not directly dependent on bile.

questions.q: A biology student in Ibadan compares the skull of a goat with that of a dog. Which dental feature is characteristic of the goat?
options: Only incisors present, with all grinding teeth absent
Sharp incisors on both upper and lower jaws for cutting grass
A diastema with flat molars adapted for grinding plant material
Large pointed canines used for tearing flesh
questions.explanation: A goat is a herbivore and has a diastema, flat molars and premolars for grinding plant material, and no upper canine teeth. Large pointed canines occur in carnivores, and goats do not have sharp incisors on both upper and lower jaws.

questions.q: A laboratory technician in Zaria observes that a dry bean seed respires very slowly, but after soaking in water and keeping it warm, its respiration rate increases markedly. Which explanation is best?
options: Warmth destroys inhibitors, causing the seed to absorb carbon dioxide.
The seed begins photosynthesis after soaking, producing oxygen.
Water prevents oxygen from entering, so anaerobic respiration immediately stops.
Water activates enzymes and warmth increases their activity, allowing respiration to proceed faster.
questions.explanation: A dry seed has very low metabolic activity; soaking allows water to activate enzymes and dissolve substrates, while warmth increases enzyme activity, so respiration rises. Photosynthesis requires chlorophyll and light and does not explain the increased respiration, and water does not cause the seed to absorb carbon dioxide.

questions.q: A community in Nasarawa State records many cases of schistosomiasis. Which activity most directly exposes people to the parasite?
options: Wading or bathing in slow-moving fresh water containing infected snails
questions.explanation: In schistosomiasis, the larval stage is released from infected freshwater snails and can penetrate the skin of people wading or bathing in contaminated water. Boiled water is safe, undercooked beef is associated with other infections, and walking barefoot on damp soil is mainly linked with hookworm infection.

questions.q: A healthy child in Aba receives a vaccine containing weakened pathogens. Which type of immunity develops?
questions.explanation: A vaccine exposes the body to weakened pathogens, stimulating it to produce its own antibodies and memory cells; this is artificial active immunity. Natural active immunity follows infection, while passive immunity involves receiving ready-made antibodies rather than producing them.

questions.q: A student in Makurdi places a crystal of blue copper(II) sulphate in a beaker of water and leaves it without stirring. After several hours, the water is uniformly blue. Which process is chiefly responsible?
questions.explanation: The particles of copper(II) sulphate move randomly from the region of higher concentration around the crystal to regions of lower concentration until they are evenly spread. This spreading without a membrane or added energy is diffusion; sedimentation would settle particles instead of making the water uniformly blue.

questions.q: Which change would most increase the rate of diffusion of a gas across a thin membrane?
options: Lowering the temperature of the system
Increasing the thickness of the membrane
Increasing the concentration gradient across the membrane
questions.explanation: The rate of diffusion increases when the concentration gradient across the membrane is steeper. Increasing membrane thickness, reducing surface area, or lowering temperature would all tend to slow diffusion rather than increase it.

questions.q: In a hospital in Ibadan, records show that babies with very low or very high birth weights survive less often than babies with average birth weight. This pattern is an example of
questions.explanation: Babies near average birth weight have the highest survival, while both extremes are selected against. This is stabilizing selection; directional selection would favour one extreme, while disruptive selection would favour both extremes.

questions.q: Chidi and Ngozi in Awka both have normal skin, but their first child is albino. Albinism is caused by a recessive allele. What are the genotypes of Chidi and Ngozi?
options: One is heterozygous (Aa) and the other is homozygous recessive (aa).
questions.explanation: For a recessive albino child to be born to parents with normal skin, each parent must carry one recessive allele, so the parents are Aa × Aa. The child receives a recessive allele from each parent; two AA parents cannot produce an aa child, and an aa parent would be albino.

questions.q: A biology student in Nsukka finds a small green plant in a damp shaded area. It has rhizoids and simple leaf-like structures but no true roots or vascular tissue. The plant is best classified as a
questions.explanation: Bryophytes such as mosses lack true roots and vascular tissue and absorb water through rhizoids. Pteridophytes have vascular tissue and true roots, stems and leaves.

questions.q: The exoskeleton of a grasshopper mainly serves to
options: allow gaseous exchange through the skin
support the body and protect internal organs
questions.explanation: The hard exoskeleton supports and protects the insect's soft internal organs and also provides attachment for muscles. It is not a main site for blood cell production, fat storage or gaseous exchange.

questions.q: A student in Ilorin studies the conversion of excess amino acids in the liver. Which waste substance is formed in the ornithine cycle during this process?
questions.explanation: Excess amino acids are deaminated in the liver to form ammonia, which is then converted to urea in the ornithine cycle. Uric acid is the main nitrogenous waste of birds and insects, while creatinine is derived from muscle creatine. Glucose is not a waste product of the ornithine cycle.

questions.q: A cyclist in Ibadan finds it difficult to keep her balance after a head injury. Which part of the brain is most likely damaged?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates muscular activity and is responsible for balance and posture. Damage to the medulla oblongata would mainly affect involuntary actions such as heartbeat and breathing, while the hypothalamus controls temperature and water balance. The cerebrum is concerned with reasoning, memory and voluntary actions.

questions.q: A woman in Benin City has just ovulated. Which hormone is secreted by the corpus luteum and prepares the uterus for implantation?
questions.explanation: After ovulation the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, which thickens and prepares the lining of the uterus for implantation. Oestrogen also acts earlier in the menstrual cycle, while follicle-stimulating hormone stimulates follicle development and luteinising hormone triggers ovulation. The corpus luteum is not the main source of follicle-stimulating hormone or luteinising hormone.

questions.q: A group of similar cells in a maize leaf work together to carry out photosynthesis. This level of organisation is called a
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function. An organ is made of different tissues, an organ system consists of several organs, and an organelle is a structure within a cell. Therefore the group of similar photosynthetic cells in the maize leaf is a tissue.

questions.q: A pond near Epe receives runoff rich in nitrate and phosphate from a nearby farm. Which change is most likely to happen first?
options: A permanent increase in dissolved oxygen
Immediate death of fish from lack of nutrients
questions.explanation: Runoff containing nitrate and phosphate adds nutrients to the pond, so algae grow rapidly in a process that can lead to eutrophication. Water transparency usually falls as the algae multiply, and oxygen may later decrease when dead algae decompose. Fish deaths can follow oxygen shortage, but they are not the first immediate change.

questions.q: A student in Jos breathes rapidly after running. Which change in the blood most directly stimulates the respiratory centre in the medulla oblongata?
options: An increase in the concentration of oxygen in the blood
A decrease in blood glucose concentration
An increase in the concentration of carbon dioxide in the blood
questions.explanation: A rise in blood carbon dioxide, with the accompanying acidity, is the main chemical stimulus to the respiratory centre. This increases the rate and depth of breathing so that excess carbon dioxide is removed. More oxygen in the blood would not stimulate breathing in the same way.

questions.q: Which structure prevents food from entering the trachea when a person in Ibadan swallows?
questions.explanation: During swallowing, the epiglottis closes over the opening of the larynx and directs food into the oesophagus. The glottis is the opening itself, while the diaphragm and pleura are associated with breathing movements and the lungs.

questions.q: A blood sample from a patient in Ibadan is analysed. Which component is chiefly responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to the tissues?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells combines with oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues. Plasma carries some dissolved oxygen, but it is not the chief oxygen carrier. White blood cells and platelets have other defensive and clotting roles.

questions.q: A patient in Aba is given a blood transfusion. Before transfusion, the patient's blood group is tested mainly to prevent which danger?
options: Destruction of white blood cells by the donor's antibodies
Excess production of platelets and rapid clotting
Agglutination of red blood cells caused by incompatible antibodies
Loss of plasma proteins through the kidneys
questions.explanation: If the donor and recipient blood groups are incompatible, antibodies in the recipient can agglutinate the donor red cells, causing a serious transfusion reaction. Blood grouping and cross-matching are therefore done before transfusion. The other effects are not the main reason for blood group testing.

questions.q: In a hibiscus flower in Enugu, after fertilisation, which structure develops into the fruit?
questions.explanation: After fertilisation, the ovary enlarges and develops into the fruit, while the ovules inside it develop into seeds. The stigma and pollen tube do not form the fruit; they wither or degenerate after fertilisation.

questions.q: During an outbreak of yellow fever in a town near Yola, a health officer advises residents to use insecticide-treated nets and screen windows. These measures are most useful because the yellow fever virus is mainly spread by
questions.explanation: Yellow fever is a viral disease transmitted mainly by the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes. Tsetse flies transmit trypanosomiasis, while houseflies and cockroaches are mainly mechanical carriers of contaminants and do not transmit the yellow fever virus.

questions.q: A school health officer in Abeokuta finds that many pupils who often walk barefooted have hookworm infection. Which practice will most directly reduce the spread of this infection?
options: Covering the mouth and nose when coughing
Sleeping under an insecticide-treated net every night
Wearing footwear and using proper sanitation facilities
questions.explanation: Hookworm larvae in contaminated soil can penetrate the skin of bare feet, and eggs are passed in human faeces, so wearing footwear and safe disposal of faeces reduce transmission. Nets, boiling drinking water and cough etiquette do not prevent hookworm infection.

questions.q: A patient in a Lagos hospital is accidentally given distilled water instead of normal saline through a drip. The red blood cells would most likely burst because
options: water enters the cells by osmosis from a dilute surrounding solution
salt is actively transported out of the cells into the plasma
water leaves the cells by osmosis into a concentrated surrounding solution
large plasma proteins diffuse through the cell membrane into the cells
questions.explanation: Distilled water has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm, so water moves into the red blood cells by osmosis until they swell and burst. The wrong ideas describe the opposite movement of water or transport of substances that cannot account for rapid bursting.

questions.q: A team studying rock layers near Sokoto finds fossils of horse-like animals with limb bones that become longer in younger rock layers. This evidence for evolution is obtained from
questions.explanation: Fossils preserved in rock layers show changes in organisms over long periods of geological time and are the evidence of the fossil record. Comparative embryology, comparative anatomy and biochemical studies use living or preserved structures and molecules, not the sequence of fossils in rock layers.

questions.q: A child in Benin City has blood group O, but both parents have blood group A. Which pair of parental genotypes can produce this child?
questions.explanation: Both A parents must be heterozygous I^A i so that each can pass an i allele to the child, giving genotype ii and blood group O. I^A I^A parents can pass only I^A, an I^A I^B parent has no i allele to pass, and ii parents would not both have blood group A.

questions.q: A farmer in Kaduna grows maize, whose scientific name is Zea mays. Which statement about this scientific name is correct?
options: Zea mays is an English name and not a scientific name.
Zea is the species and mays is the genus.
Zea is the genus and mays is the species.
Both Zea and mays are species names.
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first word of a scientific name is the genus and the second is the species. Zea is therefore the genus and mays is the species; the name is Latin-based, not an English name.

questions.q: A nurse in Jos explains that the membrane lining the capsule of a freely movable joint produces synovial fluid. What is the main function of this fluid?
options: It hardens the ends of the bones to prevent wear.
It produces red blood cells for the bones.
It joins muscle to bone at the joint.
It lubricates the joint and reduces friction between the bones.
questions.explanation: Synovial fluid is a lubricant that reduces friction between the articular surfaces in a freely movable joint. It does not produce red blood cells, attach muscle to bone, or harden the bone ends.

questions.q: A laboratory technician in Zaria examines a urine sample from a healthy person. Which substance is normally absent from the urine?
questions.explanation: In a healthy person, glucose is completely reabsorbed in the kidney tubules, so it should not appear in the urine. Urea, water and mineral salts are normal constituents of urine.

questions.q: A student in Aba steps on a sharp stone and quickly pulls his foot away. In the reflex arc, which neurone carries the impulse from the receptor toward the central nervous system?
questions.explanation: The first neurone in a reflex arc carries impulses from the receptor to the central nervous system and is the sensory neurone. Motor neurones carry impulses away from the central nervous system, while relay neurones transmit impulses within it.

questions.q: After eating a meal rich in carbohydrates, a woman in Ibadan has a high blood glucose level. Which hormone helps to lower the glucose level?
questions.explanation: Insulin is secreted by the pancreas when blood glucose is high and promotes uptake of glucose by cells and storage as glycogen. Glucagon and adrenaline raise blood glucose, while thyroxine mainly regulates metabolic rate.

questions.q: While studying cells lining the kidney tubules of a goat in Makurdi, a biology student observes many of one type of organelle. These cells use a lot of energy to reabsorb glucose by active transport. Which organelle is most abundant in such a cell?
questions.explanation: Active transport requires ATP, and mitochondria are the main site of aerobic respiration and ATP production. Chloroplasts are not found in animal cells, while ribosomes and lysosomes do not primarily supply ATP for active transport.

questions.q: Cells in the growing tip of a maize plant in Zaria become specialised into xylem, phloem and other tissues. Which statement best explains this cell differentiation?
options: Different genes are switched on or off, so different proteins are made.
Specialised cells exchange nuclei with neighbouring cells.
All cells make exactly the same proteins but in different amounts.
Each specialised cell loses a different set of chromosomes.
questions.explanation: Cell differentiation occurs because cells with the same genetic information express different genes, producing different proteins and structures for specific functions. Chromosome loss does not normally cause differentiation, and cells do not exchange nuclei to become specialised.

questions.q: Termites in Ibadan are able to feed on wood because protozoa in their gut digest cellulose, while the termites provide the protozoa with shelter and food particles. The relationship between the termites and the protozoa is best described as
questions.explanation: Mutualism is a relationship in which both organisms benefit: the protozoa digest cellulose and the termites give them shelter and food. Parasitism benefits one and harms the other, while commensalism benefits one without clearly benefiting or harming the other.

questions.q: On a newly exposed rock surface near Jos, lichens are the first organisms to grow. What is their main role in ecological succession?
options: They are primary consumers that feed on other plants.
They are the final climax community of the habitat.
They decompose dead animals and release nitrates.
They are pioneer species that help to form soil.
questions.explanation: Lichens are pioneer organisms because they can colonise bare rock; their growth and decay help form a thin soil that allows other plants to establish. They are not the climax community, nor are they primary consumers or animal decomposers.

questions.q: A state government in Nigeria wants to conserve the natural plants of a forest reserve without removing them from their habitat. Which measure is an example of in-situ conservation?
options: Growing the plants in a botanical garden far from the forest.
Protecting the plants within the forest reserve.
Storing seeds of the plants in a cold seed bank.
Keeping dried specimens of the plants in a herbarium.
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation means protecting organisms in their natural habitat, so protecting the plants within the forest reserve is an example. Seed banks, botanical gardens and herbaria conserve genetic material or specimens outside the natural habitat, which is ex-situ conservation.

questions.q: A tomato farmer in Ogoja supplies his plants with all mineral salts except magnesium. The leaves become pale because magnesium is mainly required for
questions.explanation: Magnesium is an essential part of the chlorophyll molecule, so its deficiency causes pale leaves. Calcium is more associated with cell wall strength, nitrogen with amino acid formation, and potassium with stomatal action and water regulation.

questions.q: A blood sample taken from a healthy student in Jos is analysed. Most of the carbon dioxide in the blood is carried in the form of
options: Hydrogen carbonate ions in the plasma
Carbon dioxide dissolved in the plasma
questions.explanation: About 70% of carbon dioxide is transported as hydrogen carbonate ions in the plasma after reacting with water in red blood cells. Only a smaller amount is carried as dissolved carbon dioxide or combined with haemoglobin as carbaminohaemoglobin.

questions.q: A student in Ibadan examines a cross-section of a young dicot stem. Which tissue is mainly responsible for transporting manufactured food from the leaves to the roots?
questions.explanation: Phloem tissue carries sugars and other organic solutes from leaves, where they are made, to other parts of the plant such as the roots. Xylem mainly transports water and dissolved mineral salts upward from the roots.

questions.q: A biology student in Kaduna compares the walls of arteries, veins and capillaries. Which feature of capillaries makes them best suited for exchange of materials between blood and body cells?
options: Their walls are only one cell thick.
They have valves along their length.
They have thick muscular walls with elastic fibres.
They carry blood at high pressure in a wide lumen.
questions.explanation: Capillary walls are very thin, so substances can diffuse quickly between blood and tissue cells. Arteries have thick muscular walls, while valves are characteristic of veins.

questions.q: In a hibiscus flower in Enugu, after fertilisation, the zygote develops into which structure within the seed?
questions.explanation: The zygote divides and develops into the embryo, which contains the young plant. The endosperm arises from the fertilised central cell, while the seed coat develops from the integuments.

questions.q: In a village near Kontagora, many families draw drinking water from a stream. A health officer advises boiling and cooling the water before drinking. This advice mainly helps to
options: remove suspended soil particles that make the water cloudy.
kill disease-causing organisms in the water.
increase the mineral salt content of the water.
soften hard water by removing calcium compounds.
questions.explanation: Boiling water for a sufficient time destroys many pathogens that cause water-borne diseases. It does not remove suspended particles efficiently or increase the mineral content of the water.

questions.q: A child in Lagos with whooping cough is treated with antibiotics and kept away from school for a few days. Keeping the child away from school is mainly intended to
options: replace the need for vaccination in the community.
reduce the chance of spreading the infection to other children.
prevent the child from developing fever again.
questions.explanation: Whooping cough spreads easily from an infected person to others, especially in crowded places. Keeping the child away from school reduces transmission while treatment is taking effect; antibiotics treat the infection but do not replace community vaccination.

questions.q: A small population of goats near Kontagora has only a few breeding males. Over several generations, certain coat colours become more common by chance rather than because they are better adapted. Which process is mainly responsible?
questions.explanation: Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequencies, and its effect is stronger in small populations. Natural selection would require the coat colours to give a consistent survival or reproductive advantage, which is not stated here. Mutation creates new alleles but does not by itself explain the chance increase in particular traits.
